title: hierarchical-length-hash-repacker-for-reduced-padding-and-stable-kernel-fits
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: The runtime still wastes compute and increases tail latency due to the long-tail in request sequence-length distribution. Existing fixed-seqlen bucketing reduces padding but is brittle across mixed workloads and causes kernel fit churn when sequences are repacked arbitrarily. This PR introduces a hierarchical length-hash repacker that reduces padding waste while keeping kernel launch and memory access patterns stable.

Summary of changes: Implement a two-stage batching heuristic: (1) deterministic length-hash bins that group similar-length requests but maintain pseudo-random spread to avoid pathological arrival skews, and (2) an inflight repacker that opportunistically coalesces underfilled bins using a kernel-fit scoring function. The repacker runs as a lightweight pass over in-flight slots before kernel submission, attempting bounded merges (max 2 merges per slot) to avoid excessive KV cache rewrites. To keep KV cache efficient we add a coalesced-prefetch and write path: when repacking touches requests with cached KV segments we prefetch contiguous KV ranges and commit merged writes in a single coalesced update.

Scheduling and cost model: Introduce a kernel-fit estimator that scores candidate merges based on estimated token padding reduced, estimated additional KV copy cost, and predicted kernel lane alignment. Scheduler prioritizes merges that show positive net savings under a configurable threshold (default: 1.5x padding reduction per KV-copy-cost unit). A new priority queue sorts slots by fullness/score so latency-sensitive short requests are rarely delayed.

KV cache correctness and safety: Repacking updates per-request KV pointers atomically under the existing runtime lock; we add a short-lived per-slot epoch to avoid racing writes with in-flight generation. Fallthrough exists: if prefetch fails or KV write budget is exceeded (configurable), the repacker abandons the merge and submits both slots separately to preserve correctness and latency SLOs.

Continuous batching integration: The algorithm composes with the continuous batcher by running the repacker only on fully materialized slots (i.e., when the batch window has reached submission time) to avoid destabilizing the continuous admission policy. We also added a lightweight telemetry hook so Optimize can observe pad-savings and KV overheads per model.

Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks on A100 and H100 mixes using a realistic product trace (30% short: 8-16, 50% medium: 32-64, 20% long: 256-1024) show token throughput +6% to +9% and p50 generation latency reduction 4% to 12% with p95 unchanged or slightly improved. End-to-end load tests with the dedicated capacity harness show consistent CPU/GPU occupancy improvements and reduce token-level cost estimates for the workload mix by ~5.5% in the median. Detailed bench scripts and data files are added under tests/perf.

Migration and config: New runtime flags: --length-hash-bins (default 16), --repacker-enabled (default true), --repacker-kv-budget (default 4 per-second/slot), --kernel-fit-threshold (default 1.5). All flags are runtime-configurable via the console rollout. Backwards-compatible: when disabled the system falls back to existing seqlen bucketing.

Risks & mitigations: Repacking increases KV activity; the KV budget limiter and early-abort guards ensure we do not overload the KV subsystem. We added a defensive metric (repack_aborts_due_to_kv) and an alert on any degradation in p95 and token error rates.

Files added/changed: see files_changed list. Tests: unit tests for the kernel-fit estimator, integration tests for KV prefetch paths, perf harness and traces.

Related work: builds on earlier bucketing work (ENG-2348) and the pad-trimmer experiments but takes a different tradeoff point focusing on low-overhead inflight coalescing and KV-aware merges.

Requested rollout: gradual canary across dedicated clusters for two weeks before defaulting to on for workloads with >10k reqs/day.

Notes: description and design doc are intentionally concise here; detailed design is in docs/design/length_hash_repacker.md.

review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Nice approach. Can you explain why deterministic hashing is preferable to random assignment? I worry about hot bins if traffic is correlated.

Maya Chen (reply): Deterministic length-hash keeps similar-length locality while the lower bits of the hash are mixed with a rotating nonce to avoid persistent hot bins; we've added a short section in the design doc that demonstrates the mitigation and the canary config to reduce bin count dynamically.
Priya Nair: The KV prefetch path looks reasonable but we need an extra guard around GPU memory pressure. Add a prefetch budget metric and a graceful fallback.

Maya Chen (reply): Added repacker_kv_budget flag and metric repack_prefetch_budget_exhausted_count; repacker will abort merges when budget is hit. Also added integration test to simulate prefetch failure.
Ethan Brooks: Some of the kernel-fit math seems heuristic. Can you add a comment block and a simple unit test that validates expected scoring on toy inputs?
Maya Chen (reply): Added extensive inline docs and unit tests (tests/unit/test_kernel_fit_estimator.cpp). Also included a small bench verifying estimator stability across model sizes.
